questions.question: Who can change a bus stop location?

options.text: The driver.
Parents.
The school district.

questions.correctAnswerText: The school district.
questions.explanation: The school district sets bus routes and stops. Drivers cannot change a stop without written approval from a district official.

questions.question: What is the inside rearview mirror used for?

options.text: See passengers.
See potential hazards on the road.
See vehicles trying to switch lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: See passengers.
questions.explanation: The inside rearview mirror lets you watch passengers inside the bus.

questions.question: When should you adjust mirrors on a school bus?

options.text: During the drive.
Before beginning to drive.
After the drive is completed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before beginning to drive.
questions.explanation: Check and adjust all mirrors before you start driving. Proper mirrors are important for safe bus operation.

questions.question: If a railroad crossing gate doesn't go up after a train passes, what should you do?

options.text: Drive around the gate.
Wait for another vehicle to cross first to see if it is safe.
Call your dispatcher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call your dispatcher.
questions.explanation: If a gate stays down after a train passes, call your dispatcher. Do not drive around the lowered gate.

questions.question: When should a roof-mounted strobe light be used?

options.text: In times of limited visibility.
All the time.
Only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: In times of limited visibility.
questions.explanation: Use a roof-mounted strobe light when you cannot see clearly, such as in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: How should students safely leave a bus?

options.text: Remain seated until they are told to exit.
Stand up and head toward the door while the bus is slowing down.
Exit the bus and stand directly next to it while it is being driven away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remain seated until they are told to exit.
questions.explanation: Students must stay seated until the driver tells them it is safe to exit. After leaving the bus, they should walk at least 10 feet away so the driver can see them clearly.

questions.question: Before opening the bus door to pick up students, you must ensure:

options.text: All surrounding traffic has stopped.
The alternating red lights are on.
You are pulled over to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: All surrounding traffic has stopped.
questions.explanation: Make sure all traffic around the bus has stopped before you open the door and signal for students to approach.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing during the driving test?

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is going too slow.
Get out of the vehicle to check for a train.
Do not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the railroad tracks.

questions.question: What will the examiner score you on during the driving test?

options.text: Attitude.
How quickly you arrive at your destination.
Your driving behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your driving behavior.
questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on specific driving skills and your general driving behavior.

questions.question: Why should you park at least 10 feet away from students when picking them up?

options.text: You will have a clear view of their movements.
It will be difficult to get any closer to them.
Students need to walk for exercise.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have a clear view of their movements.
questions.explanation: Park with your front bumper at least 10 feet away from students. This makes students walk to the bus, so you can watch their movements safely.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle controls skills test, where should your vehicle end up?

options.text: In the general area the examiner described.
In the exact position the examiner described.
Within three feet of the position the examiner described.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact position the examiner described.
questions.explanation: You must finish each exercise with your vehicle in the exact position the examiner described. If you do not complete the exercise exactly as instructed, you will lose points and may fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: How should a driver exit a vehicle?

options.text: Jump directly from the seat to the ground.
Keep at least one hand touching the vehicle.
Face the vehicle while exiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Face the vehicle while exiting.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must face the vehicle and use three points of contact at all times. For a bus, you must hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly will automatically fail you on the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: What do crossover mirrors help you see?

options.text: The front danger zones.
The rear bumper.
The left side of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front danger zones.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors show you the danger zone directly in front of a school bus. They also show you danger zones on the left and right sides of the bus, from the front to the service door.

questions.question: What should a school bus driver watch for as students exit?

options.text: That students are leaving in pairs.
That students do not get caught on the handrail or door.
That students do not talk while exiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: That students do not get caught on the handrail or door.
questions.explanation: Students can be injured or killed if their clothing, accessories, or bodies get caught on a handrail or door while exiting. Watch all students carefully as they exit to make sure they all leave safely and reach a safe location.

questions.question: What happens if you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: You fail only that exercise.
You lose extra points from your final score.
You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must face the vehicle and use three points of contact. For a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly will automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: When should you adjust a bus's mirrors?

options.text: Before you start operating the bus.
While you are operating the bus.
At the first stoplight after starting your shift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start operating the bus.
questions.explanation: Check and adjust mirrors before you start driving.

questions.question: When making a turn during your driving test, what should you do?

options.text: Use your turn signal only if other cars are around.
Check traffic only in the direction you are turning.
Check traffic in all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: When making a turn during your driving test, check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: How should you do a standard parallel parking maneuver?

options.text: Back up past the space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward directly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space on the right side. Then back your vehicle into the space, getting the rear as close to the back of the space as possible. Your vehicle must fit completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: Where are a school bus's danger zones?

options.text: Only in front of the bus.
Only at the rear and left side of the bus.
In front, on the sides, and at the rear of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front, on the sides, and at the rear of the bus.
questions.explanation: Danger zones are areas where children are most likely to be hit by another vehicle or the bus itself. These areas are in front, on the sides, and at the rear of a bus. Danger zones can extend 10 feet from every side of the bus.

questions.question: What does ABS (anti-lock braking system) allow a driver to do?

options.text: Drive faster.
Keep control of the vehicle while braking.
See farther ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep control of the vehicle while braking.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents your wheels from locking up and helps you maintain control when braking on slippery surfaces.
